bihar_raw_news.title: RVNL wins ₹903 crore order from SJVN Thermal for Buxar thermal power project
bihar_raw_news.content: RVNL wins ₹903 crore order from SJVN Thermal for Buxar thermal power project Shares of Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd ended at ₹212.00, up by ₹2.50, or 1.19%, on the BSE. By Jomy Jos Pullokaran September 4, 2026, 8:16:03 PM IST (Published) 2 Min Read Navratna public sector undertaking Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd on Friday (September 4) said it has received a ₹903 crore Letter of Award from SJVN Thermal Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Limited, for work related to the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project in Bihar. The order is valued at ₹903 crore, including Goods and Services Tax (GST). Under the contract, RVNL will construct a permanent siding along with an aerial connection via track from the plant boundary to Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur at Buxar, as part of Phase III of the project. The order has been awarded by a domestic entity and is in the normal course of RVNL’s business. The execution period is 36 months. RVNL said the promoter, promoter group and group companies have no interest in SJVN Thermal Private Limited. The order also does not fall under related-party transactions. ALSO READ | RVNL partners with Goa government to develop infrastructure projects in the state Yesterday, Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd has emerged as the lowest bidder for a ₹404.88-crore project from East Coast Railway, the state-owned company said in an exchange filing. The project involves a range of civil and railway infrastructure works, including construction of the roadbed and bridges, track laying, supply of ballast, buildings and road underbridges. RVNL will also undertake utility shifting, signalling and telecommunications work, electrification, power-supply arrangements and the shifting or modification of high- and low-tension electricity lines. The ₹404.88-crore contract value includes GST. ALSO READ | RVNL shares gain after winning ₹161 crore order from East Coast Railway The work is connected to the construction of a third railway line on the Nergundi-Barang and Khurda Road-Vizianagaram stretches. Together, the two stretches cover 385 km — 22 km between Nergundi and Barang and 363 km between Khurda Road and Vizianagaram. Adding a third line can increase a railway corridor's capacity by allowing it to handle more passenger and freight trains and reducing congestion on existing tracks. RVNL has emerged as the L1, or lowest, bidder for the project. Being L1 typically puts the company in pole position for the contract, but it isn't the same as receiving the final Letter of Acceptance. Shares of Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd ended at ₹212.00, up by ₹2.50, or 1.19%, on the BSE. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Promotes Aquaculture Insurance Under PM-MKSSY - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Promotes Aquaculture Insurance Under PM-MKSSY 04 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar is promoting aquaculture insurance for fish farmers under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) , providing financial support on insurance premiums and additional benefits for SC, ST and women fish farmers . Key Points Insurance Support: Fish farmers can receive a 40% one-time incentive on insurance premiums , up to ₹1 lakh . SC, ST and women beneficiaries can receive an additional 10% incentive , taking the maximum benefit to ₹1.10 lakh . Insurance Coverage: Insurance coverage can extend up to ₹20 lakh , depending on the premium paid. Eligible Area: For the one-time incentive, eligible water-spread area is calculated at ₹25,000 per hectare , with a maximum limit of 4 hectares . The scheme covers ponds, aquaculture farms, RAS, cages, bio-floc and raceway systems. Covers risks such as floods, cyclones, pollution, drought and other natural disasters. Bihar’s Fish Production: Fish production increased from 9.69 lakh metric tonnes in 2024-25 to 10.28 lakh metric tonnes in 2025-26 . The state has 233 fish seed hatcheries , meeting around 70% of its fish seed requirement . Bihar has 89 fish feed mills , producing around 50,000 tonnes of fish feed locally . Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY): Nature: Implemented as a Central Sector Sub-scheme under the Central Sector Component of PMMSY . Outlay: ₹6,000 crore. Public Finance: ₹3,000 crore (50%) , including World Bank and AFD external financing . Beneficiary/Private Investment: ₹3,000 crore (50%) through anticipated beneficiary and private-sector investment. Duration: 4 years , from FY 2023-24 to FY 2026-27 . Advertisment Karnataka spent the last decade turning an early lead into outright dominance. Bihar spent it almost entirely on the sidelines, and is only now, in the last two years, showing the first real signs of a state that intends to catch up. bihar_raw_news.title: India's scheme for rare earth magnet production gains broad industry participation: Report
bihar_raw_news.content: International 03 Sep, 2026 India's scheme for rare earth magnet production gains broad industry participation: Report Business To Business, New Delhi, 03 September 2026: India has received 20 bids to build integrated rare‑earth permanent magnet manufacturing facilities and the government aims to create an integrated chain stretching from NdPr oxide to finished magnets, a new report has said. The report from Times Kuwait highlighted that India’s broader critical-mineral strategy increasingly focuses on value addition, processing and manufacturing rather than stopping at the extraction stage. The warm response by bidders to the initiative has given fresh momentum to a policy effort that goes beyond securing a raw material to forming industrial capacity necessary to convert India’s rare-earth resources into high-value products for the country's fastest-growing sector, the report said. India's $7.74 billion rare‑earth permanent scheme aims to create 6,000 metric tonnes per annum of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity in India. Ministry of Heavy Industries invited proposals on March 20, 2026 and opened technical bids on August 13, 2026, as companies including Larsen & Toubro, Coal India, ReNew, Attero Recycling, 20 Microns, Lohum Magnets & Energy Solutions, NEO Performance Materials of Singapore and Proterial India responded. “Twenty companies and consortia submitted bids, bringing together established engineering companies, public-sector enterprises, recycling specialists, energy companies, magnet manufacturers and international participants,” the publication said. The scheme targets up to five beneficiaries, selected through global competitive bidding, each eligible for as much as 1,200 metric tonnes per annum. The scheme design places production at the centre of the programme, the report said, adding that it connects government support to the actual manufacture and sale of magnets rather than focusing solely on creating facilities. The publication mentioned broad participation of firms from different industrial backgrounds as evidence of rare-earth processing and magnet manufacturing being viewed as a wider industrial opportunity. India’s policy emphasis is now shifting towards connecting substantial rare-earth resources with industrial value chains. Government assessments indicated a huge gap between upstream capabilities and industrial-scale midstream and downstream manufacturing. The timing of the rare-earth push is also closely connected to India’s broader technology and manufacturing ambitions along with advances in mobile phones and electronics exports, Permanent magnets sit at the intersection of many of these sectors including semiconductors, electric mobility, renewable energy equipment and advanced manufacturing. bihar_raw_news.title: Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP over youth protests | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 03, 2026 Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP against suppressing voice of youth Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi interacts with students from Bihar injured during protests against alleged irregularities in examination system, at his residence, in New Delhi. (@RahulGandhi/X via PTI Photo) Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday backed students and youngsters in Bihar who protested against alleged irregularities in the examination system, and warned the BJP that any government that suppresses the voice of the youth will eventually have to answer to the people. Gandhi made the remarks after meeting students and young people who, he said, had faced “horrific police brutality” while raising their concerns over the examination system. “Police lathis as well as gunfire from AK-47 and pistols left many students injured. A young man aspiring to serve the country in the Army had his leg battered by an AK-47 bullet -- and with it, his life-long dream was also shattered,” Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. He said the protesters were only demanding fair opportunities, a transparent examination system and their rights. “What was the need to use lathis and bullets in response to such demands?” Gandhi asked. He also rejected any attempt to hold only lower-ranking officials responsible for the police action. “The government cannot absolve itself of responsibility for such extreme brutality by merely blaming a few low-ranking officials. This action is either the result of orders from above or a sign of the administration's utter failure,” he said. Gandhi said he stood with the protesting youngsters and was ready to provide them with all possible assistance. “The BJP should remember: any regime that suppresses the voice of the youth eventually has to answer to the people. That day is not far off,” he said. Patna witnessed clashes between job aspirants and police last month after protesters tried to march towards the chief minister’s residence, demanding a single-tier teacher recruitment examination and a transparent recruitment process. The students’ agitation, which began in the first week of August, has received support from opposition leaders, including RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: How a 57-YO Barrage Helped Shield Bihar From the Nepal Himalayan Flood Surge
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Sustainability How a 57-YO Barrage Helped Shield Bihar From the Nepal Himalayan Flood Surge How a 57-YO Barrage Helped Shield Bihar From the Nepal Himalayan Flood Surge As floodwaters from Nepal surged towards Bihar, engineers opened all 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. By TBI Team 04 Sep 2026 As floodwaters from Nepal surged towards Bihar, engineers opened all 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. By TBI Team 04 Sep 2026 Follow Us New Update As the flood surge intensified, engineers opened all 36 gates of the barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. On 26 August, catastrophic floods swept through parts of Nepal, leaving hundreds dead and thousands missing as swollen rivers tore through communities. Advertisment The floodwaters surged through the Trishuli and Narayani river systems before entering India as the Gandak. As the Himalayan disaster moved towards Bihar, the state faced the threat of a massive influx of water. Advertisment Add The Better India As A Trusted Source At Valmikinagar, however, engineers had a crucial piece of infrastructure on their side: the 57-year-old Gandak Barrage. As the flood surge intensified, engineers opened all 36 gates of the barrage, releasing nearly 1.5 lakh cusecs of water in a controlled manner. The aim was to manage the enormous volume of water flowing downstream and prevent an even more destructive surge from overwhelming the region. The intervention did come at a cost. Low-lying areas of West Champaran were flooded, agricultural fields went underwater , and families had to be evacuated from vulnerable areas. But the barrage helped regulate the incoming water at a critical moment, potentially reducing the impact of the Himalayan flood surge on downstream communities. View this post on Instagram Without such regulation, an unchecked surge could have inundated larger stretches of Bihar, damaged vast areas of farmland and deposited huge quantities of Himalayan silt across the plains. Communities in vulnerable areas would also have had far less time to respond. Built to manage the worst The Gandak Barrage was constructed as part of the 1959 Gandak Agreement between India and Nepal, with the broader Gandak river system being developed to regulate water and support irrigation across the region. Located at Valmikinagar in West Champaran, the barrage has spent decades controlling the flow of one of the major rivers entering Bihar from the Himalayan region. Its importance becomes particularly evident during extreme weather events, when enormous volumes of water can move rapidly from the mountains into the plains. More than half a century after it was built , the barrage once again became a critical line of defence when a Himalayan flood disaster reached India's doorstep. For the communities downstream, it was a reminder that infrastructure built decades ago can play a crucial role when nature unleashes its most powerful forces. bihar_raw_news.title: Foodgrain production estimated at 376.5 million tonnes amid robust decentralised grain storage infra
bihar_raw_news.content: Business 03 Sep, 2026 Foodgrain production estimated at 376.5 million tonnes amid robust decentralised grain storage infra Business To Business, New Delhi, 03 September 2026: The country’s total foodgrain production is estimated at 376.563 million tonnes, according to the Third Advance Estimates (2025-26), which is nearly 18.8 million tonnes (5.3 per cent) higher than last year’s production of 357.732 million tonnes, an official factsheet said on Thursday. India also operates one of the world’s largest food security programmes under the National Food Security Act, 2013, that covers about 80 crore people. “India’s expanding agricultural production and food security efforts have increased the importance of decentralised grain storage infrastructure across the country. The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, launched in 2023, is designed to improve storage, processing, procurement, and distribution systems through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS),” the factsheet noted. The plan is supported through institutional coordination and financial support mechanisms. Beginning with pilot projects across 11 states/PACS with 9,750 MT of storage capacity, the initiative has expanded steadily. As of July 2026, godown construction had been completed in 313 PACS across the country, creating more than 1.80 LMT of storage capacity. The framework also emphasises quality standards, transparency and operational viability, according to the factsheet. The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector seeks to reduce foodgrain wastage and strengthen food security; provide farmers with greater flexibility to avoid distress sales and secure better price realization; reduce transportation costs between procurement centres, warehouses, and Fair Price Shops; and expand the role of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) through diversification of agricultural activities. It also supports higher income opportunities for farmers. The pilot projects were implemented in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Assam, Karnataka, and Tripura. These pilots have provided an important operational foundation and demonstrated the feasibility of local storage infrastructure at the cooperative level, said the factsheet. According to the official statement, the Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector represents an integrated approach towards improving agricultural infrastructure through cooperatives. By linking storage, processing, procurement, and distribution at the PACS level, the Plan strengthens foodgrain management closer to production centres. national_raw_news.content: The festival of Janmashtami, marking the birth of Lord Krishna, is being celebrated across the country with religious fervour today. On the occasion, devotees observe fasts, perform ceremonies and visit temples. Sweets and other foods associated with Krishna are prepared and offered to Lord Krishna. Devotional songs and chanting are performed throughout the day and often late into the night. Temples and homes have been decorated with scenes depicting episodes from Krishna’s life, such as his childhood in Gokul and Vrindavan. Akashvani Uttar Pradesh Correspondent reports that the city of Lord Krishna, Mathura-Vrindavan, is decked up for the grand celebration tonight. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will take part in Janmashtami celebrations in Mathura today. In view of the huge crowd of devotees coming from across the country and abroad, extensive security arrangements have been made in the city. President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to citizens on Janmashtami. In her message, the President said the life and teachings of Lord Krishna breathe new life into India’s cultural and philosophical heritage. She said Lord Krishna’s teachings, embodied in the Shrimad Bhagavad Gita, remain an eternal source of inspiration for humanity to make prudent decisions during difficult times and remain steadfast in moral values. The President said Janmashtami inspires everyone to uphold the spirit of harmony and devotion to duty and service. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also extended greetings to the people on Janmashtami. He said devotion and love for Lord Shri Krishna are boundless among his countless devotees in India and across the world. Mr Birla said the profound wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita offers timeless guidance on duty, ethics, justice, wisdom, courage and balance in life.

national_raw_news.title: Ramdas Athawale inaugurates distribution of NAMASTE Cards to waste pickers in MCD ...
national_raw_news.content: Ramdas Athawale inaugurates distribution of NAMASTE Cards to waste pickers in MCD Najafgarh zone Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Ramdas Athawale inaugurates distribution of NAMASTE Cards to waste pickers in MCD Najafgarh zone ANI | Updated: Sep 04, 2026 15:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 4 (ANI): Ramdas Athawale , Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, inaugurated the issuance of National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Cards to waste pickers of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) Najafgarh Zone at a programme held at the MCD Community Hall in the National Capital on Friday. According to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the event marked a significant step in the formal recognition and empowerment of waste pickers under the NAMASTE scheme, aimed at improving the safety, dignity, and socio-economic status of sanitation workers across the country. Alongside the NAMASTE Cards, the Minister also distributed Ayushman Cards among the waste pickers present, extending healthcare coverage benefits to this vital workforce. In his address, Athawale lauded the tireless contribution of waste pickers in keeping Indian cities clean, describing their work as essential to the nation's sanitation and public health efforts. He assured the workers of the Government's full cooperation and continued support in improving their working conditions and access to welfare schemes, the Ministry said. More than 300 waste pickers from the Najafgarh Zone participated in the programme. The NAMASTE is a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, implemented to ensure the safety, dignity, and socio-economic upliftment of sanitation workers, including sewer and septic tank workers and waste pickers. The scheme focuses on occupational safety, formal recognition of workers, access to healthcare and social security benefits, skill development, and mechanisation of hazardous sanitation work, with the aim of eliminating hazardous manual cleaning practices across the country. A EUPHORIC narrative about India’s strong growth performance started getting constructed as soon as the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) put out the estimates of GDP for Q1 or the first quarter (April-June) of 2026-27 on August 31, 2026. The very next day, the Press Information Bureau (PIB) posted a backgrounder on India’s GDP performance, which boldly asserted that “India’s economy began 2026-27 on a strong note, with real GDP growth accelerating to 7.8% in Q1 ” and further claimed that this was “the highest Q1 real GDP growth during the four-year period from 2023-24 to 2026-27” . The MoSPI’s original August 31, 2026, release through the PIB contained the following line: “Real GDP has been estimated to grow by 7.8% in Q1 of FY 2026-27 against the growth rate of 6.9% experienced during Q1 of FY 2025-26”. For those who remember August 29, 2025, when the GDP estimates for Q1 of 2025-26 were announced, there might be sense of deja vu because that press release of a year ago stated that “Real GDP has been estimated to grow by 7.8% in Q1 of FY 2025-26 over the growth rate of 6.5% during Q1 of FY 2024-25”. So, 7.8 per cent this year is great and represents an ‘acceleration’ because what was originally a quarterly GDP growth of 7.8 per cent last year has now been revised downward to 6.9 per cent. One might legitimately ask what’s the excitement all about and how do we know this year’s 7.8 per cent will not eventually also be revised downward? The Government might of course insist that the current year’s figures are based on the new GDP series which incorporate ‘improved’ methods of estimating GDP. The September 1, PIB Backgrounder in fact claimed that “Real GDP has been revised upwards for the previous three financial years. The revisions show that the first-quarter performance follows a stronger growth trajectory than previously estimated.” The first part of the statement is entirely meaningless and the second is completely false. What is referred to as ‘Real GDP’ is simply the GDP of any year estimated on the basis of the actual prices prevailing in that year (GDP at current prices or nominal GDP) converted into an estimate of what it would be if all prices were the same as that in some common base year. It is used only for purposes of separating the ‘real growth’ from the change in nominal GDP that is simply on account of changes in prices. national_raw_news.content: Live Chennai: IPPB Introduces Mutual Fund and Insurance Services: Invest from Home, Invest from Home, IPPB mutual fund, IPPB insurance services, India Post Payments Bank, digital investment, mutual funds, insurance policies Buy Leads | Sell gold for cash in Chennai | Power Shutdown Areas in Chennai - Saturday (05-09-2026) | Chennai Metro to Follow Saturday Timetable on September 4 for Krishna Jayanthi IPPB Introduces Mutual Fund and Insurance Services: Invest from Home Updated: 04/Sep/2026 2:05:12 PM 2575 views PREV NEXT India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) has introduced digital mutual fund and insurance services for its customers as part of its 9th anniversary celebrations. Customers who wish to invest can now do so easily through digital channels. They can also access insurance policy services online. IPPB made these announcements on September 1. The information was also confirmed by the government news agency, the Press Information Bureau (PIB) . Customers can now use digital services from the comfort of their homes to invest in mutual fund schemes and purchase insurance policies. With options such as life insurance, health insurance and general insurance , customers will no longer have to visit different offices to access these two services. The bank has stated that it is expanding its services beyond financial transactions to include investments and financial protection. Mutual fund and insurance services will now be added to the list of digital services available to IPPB account holders. However, PIB has not specified which mutual fund schemes will be available or which insurance companies` policies will be offered through the platform. There is also no information yet regarding the fees and commissions that will be charged to customers. More details are expected to be announced in the coming days. IPPB Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer R. Viswesvaran said that the bank is expanding its digital services to help ordinary customers invest in suitable investment schemes and obtain insurance policies more easily. As of March 31, 2026, IPPB had a total of 13.25 crore customers , of whom 77% were from rural areas. The new service has been introduced with these customers in mind. Customers have deposited a total of ₹29,104 crore with the bank so far. IPPB`s services are being provided across 5.57 lakh villages and towns through 1.65 lakh post offices and 3 lakh post office employees. In addition, IPPB has introduced services such as SHG savings accounts for self-help groups and rural micro-entrepreneurs. Customers holding Surakshit Savings Accounts are also provided insurance coverage of up to ₹25,000 in case of online fraud. national_raw_news.content: Ahmedabad media delegation visits Biotech Park Kathua - Daily Excelsior Menu Todays story Latest News State Business National International Letters Editorials Sunday Magazine State National Business Opinion Sports International Sunday Magazine J&K Govt Orders Videos Amarnath Yatra Ahmedabad based media delegation during visit to Biotech Park Kathua on Thursday. Excelsior Correspondent KATHUA, Sept 3: Ahmedabad based media delegation which is on tour to J&K, locally coordinated by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), visited the Industrial Biotech Park (IBTP), Kathua, to see the biotechnology, startup and agriculture-related initiatives being implemented through CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (CSIR-IIIM), Jammu. The visit was part of the delegation's ongoing press tour of CSIR-IIIM and its associated facilities, showcasing the institute's work in taking scientific research from laboratories to farmers, startups, industry and society. The delegation was briefed about the BioNEST Bioincubation Centre and Centre of Excellence (CoE) at IBTP Kathua, which provide support to technology-based startups and innovators through scientific facilities, mentorship and infrastructure for product development, testing and validation. Dr Saurabh Saran, PI, BioNEST IIIM-TBI, spoke about the incubation and entrepreneurship activities being carried out through the institute. Dr Suphla B Gupta, Nodal Aroma Mission, apprised the delegation about the Aroma Mission and Floriculture Mission of CSIR-IIIM and the institute's work with farmers in medicinal and aromatic plants. She also highlighted CSIR-IIIM's efforts to provide farmers with scientific guidance and technical support at different stages of cultivation. Dr Amit Nargotra, Scientist-F, briefed the delegation on the scope of Artificial Intelligence-driven innovations. Earlier, Dr Ajaz Ahmad Mir, CEO, BioNEST Bioincubation Centre, IBTP, made a detailed presentation on the BioNEST Bioincubation Centre and the Centre of Excellence at Kathua. He apprised the visiting journalists of the facilities available for emerging entrepreneurs and innovators, particularly in biotechnology, agriculture, nutrition and health. The delegation was also informed about the wider startup ecosystem of CSIR-IIIM. The media delegation later visited laboratory facilities at IBTP. The visit was followed by a tour of the Biofarm at IBTP, giving the journalists a first-hand view of field-level applications of scientific interventions and the institute's efforts to connect laboratory research with agriculture. The programme concluded with interactions between the visiting media professionals and CSIR-IIIM scientists and officials, followed by a vote of thanks by Dr Vidushi Abrol, Business Manager, IIIM-TBI. Excelsior Sports Correspondent JAMMU, Sept 3: The official poster of the North Zone Muay Thai Championship 2026 was launched by Neha Jalali, Director, Press Information Bureau (PIB) Jammu. The championship is scheduled to be held on October 24 and 25 at the University of Jammu. Organized by the Muay Thai Association of Jammu & Kashmir (MAJK) and approved by the United Muay Thai Association of India (UMAI), the event is expected to attract athletes and teams from various North Indian states. Chief Patron Sahil Aggarwal and MAJK President Amit Singh were present on the occasion. The organizers thanked Jalali for her support and encouragement towards promoting Muay Thai and sports in Jammu & Kashmir. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Commerce & Industry Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Nationwide FTA Utilisation Drive to Expand India’s Global Trade Footprint India’s nine FTAs spanning economies with about $60 trillion GDP to provide preferential access to nearly two-thirds of global trade: Shri Goyal Combined with upcoming FTAs and efforts to deepen market access, India could gain access to 75% of global trade at rates lower than competitors India’s exports reach about $317 billion during April-July, up by $36-37 billion over corresponding period last year Calls for FTA outreach to reach every district, MSME, trader, entrepreneur, startup and woman entrepreneur Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today called for a focused, inclusive and nationwide effort to maximise the utilisation of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to expand India’s trade across the world and ensure that the benefits of enhanced market access reach businesses across the country. Addressing the National Workshop on “Leveraging FTAs an Outreach Programme” in New Delhi today, Shri Goyal emphasised the need for a concerted effort to translate India’s expanding network of FTAs into greater export opportunities for businesses across the country. Shri Goyal said the initiative should rapidly take roots across the country and reach the last person, smallest business person, trader, entrepreneur, startup and woman entrepreneur across all 780 districts, big and small. He said every contribution, big or small, would be invaluable in achieving the larger objective of transforming India from a largely inward-looking domestic economy into an international player of significance. The day-long workshop brought together senior officials from the Central Government, States and Union Territories, Export Promotion Councils and industry associations, with the objective of translating India’s expanding network of Free Trade Agreements into measurable outcomes for Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs and first-time exporters. The Minister said India should become an economy recognised and respected across the world for its contributions and a trusted partner of the world. He said this trust should translate into value and that this value proposition should emerge from collective efforts across the country towards making India a $30 trillion economy by 2047, with a very large share of international trade. Shri Goyal said India was passing through an important phase of its economic journey and highlighted the first-quarter GDP growth of 7.8% at constant prices. He said achieving 7.8% GDP growth amid uncertainty and tremendous turmoil around the world was a significant achievement. He urged people not to be guided by the “naysayers”. The Minister said the GDP numbers were not made by the government, ministers or bureaucrats, but were determined through an elaborate, ground-up and independent process run by the Ministry of Statistics, which has been in place for decades. The Minister called for continued, consistent, relentless and outcome-oriented efforts, with greater inclusion to take the entire country along, encourage new entrepreneurs to look at global markets and utilise the tremendous opportunities that have opened up.
